question: Which remaining CALABARZON waterbody leads have explicitly source-named locality contexts that can be linked to a working PSA PSGC city or municipality code without inferring a route or boundary?
method: Reviewed the source locality wording already transcribed on each scoped waterbody and the linked source crosswalk, then attached only exact named locality labels to their enumerated 10-digit PSGC city or municipality codes. Replaced broad province-only associations with source-locality-specific rows where one source named several localities. No route, polygon, boundary, species, or public record was inferred.

notAssignedThisBatch.reason: The receiving-river relationship is described, but the reviewed wording does not directly name a municipality-locality for this river itself; no code is inferred from the waterbody name or the Sakang source municipality.
The river/watershed-council context does not resolve the river locality to a municipality-level channel reach in the reviewed source text.
The principal basin and same-named river remain distinct; a river or council name does not allocate the basin to Macalelon municipality.
Reviewed sources disagree on whether the watercourse is in San Andres only or also San Francisco; preserve the conflict pending source adjudication.
Monitoring and fishery sources provide site context, not a defensible municipal allocation or gulf boundary.
The source describes protected-landscape context but does not assign each river reach to an individual municipality.

nonClaims: A city/municipality code records a source-described locality or assessment-area relationship only; it is not a river route, watershed boundary, polygon, coordinate, fishing ground, access right, or legal municipal-water boundary.
Watershed and administrative-boundary relationships are labeled as such and do not imply that a whole channel or basin lies in every linked municipality.
No species assertion, current presence/absence, catchability, diet, safety, water-quality, fishing-rule, or public admission claim was created.
The 158-lead CALABARZON waterbody inventory remains incomplete and scopeFrozen remains false; the PSGC denominator is not a waterbody inventory.
City-coded and municipality-coded lead counts may overlap for a multi-locality waterbody; they are not mutually exclusive groups.
nextAction: Continue the source-backed locality review across the 106 province-only leads, separately resolve the four leads without any locality code, reconcile missing waterbodies and shared-water relationships, and seek route-scale geometry only from sources with reusable terms.
